newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Big offering seen weighing on Australian wool.
newsitem.headline: Big offering seen weighing on Australian wool.

text.p: A big offering at this week's Australian wool sales in Sydney and Melbourne is likely to weigh on the market, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said.

"Supply will be greater again this week, with an extra 30,000 bales rostered for sale, likely to have a dampening effect on market strength and cause prices to fluctuate or perhaps tend lower," Wesfarmers said in a market commentary.
However, the longer term outlook remained positive with demand expected to outstrip supply this season, supported by generally favourable exchange rates, it said.
About 92,000 bales are rostered for sale this week.

The Australian Council of Wool Exporters said offerings in the coming weeks are expected to be much higher than normal for this time of year with grower stocks coming onto the market and shearing well advanced because of the dry winter.
In addition, Europe is in its summer holidays and Chinese orders are relatively quiet as importers wait to see the price trend in coming weeks, it said.
The eastern market indicator rose two cents to 718 cents a kg clean last week at the first sales of the 1997/98 season.
